A1.justification: Both PDFs describe StarEmbed and provide readable main text, figures, tables, and appendices. Retained content can be matched reliably across the additions and renumbering.

before.justification: Tables 4–6 report original clustering, classification, and out-of-distribution detection results. Appendix C reports an original ZTF–MACHO embedding analysis.

after.justification: Original benchmark experiments remain, supplemented by dataset diagnostics, feature importance, Moirai fine-tuning, and period-regression results.

M1.justification: The main benchmark retains frozen pretrained encoders. Appendix E additionally fine-tunes Moirai-small using masked-token prediction, introducing a limited model-adaptation procedure absent from v1, without a new architecture.

E1.justification: Appendix F and Table 9 add period regression, extending evaluation to prediction of a continuous physical parameter. v1 mentioned period estimation only as future work. The existing ZTF/CSPVS coverage and MACHO comparison remain.

E2.justification: The retained experiments use the same embedding models, handcrafted features, random embeddings, and classifier heads. The new regression table uses a subset of existing comparators. Its Lomb–Scargle comparison claim is not accompanied by a reported baseline score.

E3.justification: Existing splits, filtering, embedding sizes, and classifier settings remain unchanged. New protocols include fine-tuning on approximately one million ZTF light curves for 24 hours and evaluating period regression with RMSE and R². The regression head and task-specific splits are not specified.

E4.justification: v2 adds sampling-frequency and measurement-uncertainty diagnostics, a timestamp-versus-measurement-index case study, random-forest feature importance, and Moirai fine-tuning loss analysis. Period regression further probes whether embeddings preserve periodicity. The earlier Astromer-collapse analysis remains.

E5.justification: Confusion-matrix averaging changes from three RF/MLP runs in v1 Appendix D to ten runs in v2 Appendix G. However, Table 6 still specifies three seeds, 42, 100, and 200, leaving the replication underlying the updated table results unresolved.

E6.justification: Tables 4–6 and appendix matrices contain revised results: Chronos-tiny K-means F1 changes from 0.3410 to 0.3110, Astromer-2 MLP F1 from 0.388 to 0.470, and Chronos-Bolt top-10-percentile OOD purity from 0.528 to 0.519. New results include period regression, feature importance, and fine-tuning loss. Astromer panels are corrected and reassigned. The run-reporting inconsistency limits attribution of stochastic-score changes.

T1.justification: No formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or mathematical derivations are added or revised. The new feature-importance explanation describes a standard empirical calculation rather than introducing theoretical results.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the benchmark, generalization, and OOD-performance claims. The conclusion qualifies the proposed paradigm shift by linking its realization to future models that handle irregular sampling and include such data in pretraining.

C2.justification: The revised conclusion attributes important limitations to discarded timestamp information and consequent loss of periodic structure, connecting this explanation to feature importance and period regression. Appendix E adds an interpretation of the fine-tuning plateau and argues that adaptation requires further design. These substantially expand the discussion of mechanisms and applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: v2 documents the new fine-tuning objective, approximate dataset size, duration, and training trajectory, and explains the weighted impurity-decrease calculation for feature importance. Existing implementation tables and access information remain unchanged. Fine-tuning hyperparameters and the regression implementation remain insufficiently documented.

R1.justification: Five cited works are added: Dubath et al. (2011), Kim and Bailer-Jones (2016), Sesar et al. (2017), Edwards et al. (2024), and J.-S. Pan et al. (2024). They modestly extend discussion of feature-based classification, period importance, and TSFM scaling; the principal novelty positioning remains.

P1.justification: Section 6 is rewritten, Section 3 gains explanatory paragraphs, and new Appendices D–F precede the former confusion-matrix appendix, now G. Authorship and contribution statements also change. Most existing prose and the main section order remain intact.

P2.justification: Four new figures display dataset distributions, timestamp distortion, feature importance, and fine-tuning loss; Table 9 adds regression results. Appendix confusion matrices also receive class-label corrections and replacement or reassignment of Astromer panels. Existing UMAP and embedding-alignment figures are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: The added diagnostics and period probing better explain the benchmark's limitations, while corrected Astromer panels resolve misleading displays in v1. These benefits are limited by underspecified regression methods, fine-tuning conclusions based only on training loss, and inconsistent reporting: Appendix G specifies ten runs, Table 6 retains three seeds, and Figure 3 retains older classification values. The net gain is useful but limited.
